title: Task edge proposal
description: The edge file the task-dependency-mapper writes for ONE Task created outside elaboration, in the task-dependency-assessment workflow: the candidate <workDir>/candidates/edges.json, which jsonartifact.py validates against this file and publishes as <workDir>/edges.json. `depscore.py validate` then checks it against the tracker and `depscore.py apply-edges` applies it as beads `blocks` edges; the workflow writes `elements` into the Task's `matrix_elements` metadata key when the Task states no id. Nothing in it is written into the matrix. The same agent's elaboration hand-off is a different contract, task-deps.schema.json.

edges.description: EVERY edge to or from the assessed Task that passes the test (one Task consumes what the other provides: an API, a table, an IAM grant, a deployed resource), each owned standing edge it keeps included, and no edge that does not touch it. No edge is a valid result.

withdrawn.description: Every owned standing edge (the context's `standing` with `owned: true`) that `edges` does not keep. An edge with `owned: false` is in neither list.

elements.description: [] when the context's `task.elements` is not empty. Otherwise the matrix ids the session named for the Task: its stack first, then the entries it builds and the shared capabilities it uses, each the id of an entry the matrix holds; [] only when the matrix holds no stack for what the Task builds, which the reasoning states.

Edge.description: One build dependency: `to` cannot be built until `from` is built, because `to` consumes something `from` provides. Both ends are open Tasks.

from.description: The beads id of the Task built first.

to.description: The beads id of the Task that consumes what `from` provides.

reason.description: The artifact consumed and which Task provides it.

answers.description: Required only on an edge the context's `withdrawn` list covers: why the recorded withdrawal reason is wrong. Without it that edge is refused.
